topic.title: The sunroof ladder
topic.claim: The sunroof you'll open twice a year is how carmakers get you from the variant you needed to the one you bought.
topic.moment: At the showroom, the one feature you want only comes in the top two variants.

turn.believed: Top variants are for people who want all the features.
turn.actually: One visible feature is kept for the top end so you buy everything that comes with it.

topic.feeling: I paid lakhs extra for one thing other people can see.
topic.villain: Variant bundling that locks the visible features to the costliest trims
topic.because: Features people can see from the road sell better than safety or engines. Putting them only in top trims raises what the average buyer spends.
topic.payoff: Test: list the features you paid for and tick the ones you used this month.
topic.behaviour: Buyers go two variants up for a sunroof or a big screen, and brands bundle those features only at the top.
topic.mechanism: Visible features drive the upgrade, so they're used as bait for the whole bundle.
topic.group: First-time car buyers in their late 20s and early 30s
topic.send_to: The friend who's comparing variants this week
topic.why_now: Festive car-buying season just ended with record bookings.

score.why: Everyone who has stood in a showroom knows the one feature that only comes in the top trim. It shows we pay for what others can see, and the reader can test it on their own car.
